question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, who can contribute to the corpus of a Category III AIF?

answer.text: Indian, foreign, and NRI investors — with minimum investment of INR 1 crore per investor (INR 25 lakh for employees/directors of AIF or Manager), corpus minimum INR 20 crore, and maximum 1000 investors per scheme.
Only individual HNIs with minimum investment of INR 50 lakh.
Only foreign portfolio investors with RBI approval.

explanation.text: The Logic: Indian, foreign, and NRI investors can all contribute to an AIF corpus. The minimum investment per investor is INR 1 crore (INR 25 lakh for employees/directors of the AIF or Manager). Each scheme must have a minimum corpus of INR 20 crore. Maximum investors per scheme = 1000. Capital is raised only through private placement. Accredited Investors enjoy flexibility on the minimum investment amount. The Trap: Option B wrongly excludes foreign/NRI investors. Option C understates the INR 1 crore minimum. Option D wrongly narrows eligibility to FPIs. Note: The INR 1 crore minimum (or INR 25 lakh for employees/directors), INR 20 crore corpus minimum, 1,000-investor cap, and private-placement requirement apply uniformly to Category I, II, and III AIFs.
